rules.rule: Do not take breaking changes (behavioral or binary) unless their value clearly outweighs the risk to existing users; justify any you propose.
Public API shape is frozen within a major version: e.g. changing a public field to a property is binary breaking and not allowed.

Serialized output must stay compatible across versions and identical across platforms/targets; a change that silently alters the bytes produced for existing types is rejected or needs a read-both-forms migration.
Deserialization must not overwrite values the type itself set (constructor or initializer) when a member is missing from the data, and should fail loudly rather than quietly return null.
Keep the AOT (source-generated) and dynamic resolver behavior equivalent; a change to one must be matched in the other.
Never hand-edit generated .cs files; change the .tt template (or generator) and regenerate.
Keep logic out of T4 templates and do not add unnecessary dependencies to the generator; a clean code base outranks micro-savings in tooling.
Performance claims need evidence: an optimization attribute or refactor that does not change compiled output or regresses benchmarks is not accepted.
Features with a significant performance cost must be opt-in, not on by default.
Optional or platform-specific integrations (e.g. Unity.Mathematics) go in a separate assembly/asmdef and their own resolver, never into StandardResolver or the core assembly.
Prefer a small internal static helper over sprinkling #if blocks through code for trivial checks such as throw helpers.
Avoid formatter-specific members on MessagePackSerializerOptions and virtual hooks whose effect depends on which options instance is seen first.
Do not add target frameworks lightly, and do not assume a TFM (e.g. netstandard2.1) implies a particular runtime such as Unity; tools must keep working on the SDKs users already have.
Target feature work at the active branch (develop at the time) rather than master; changes that merge only to master and conflict with develop are reverted or declined.
Bug fixes and new analyzer/generator cases need a test covering the case.
Discuss larger or design-level changes in an issue first; PRs whose linked issue goes unanswered, or that are superseded by a broader maintainer fix, get closed.
The serializer handles instance data only; out-of-scope features (static members, guaranteed map key ordering) are declined in favor of custom formatters.
Value types used for change detection must implement GetHashCode consistently with their custom Equals (including array fields).
APIs that have not shipped yet belong in PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt; changing unshipped API is not a breaking change.
Prefer complete, maintainable fixes over minimal patches (e.g. a version bump or a partial package-ref suppression).
